paragraphs: The AI/ML Marine Plastic Debris Monitoring System (also titled Indian Ocean Shield) is an end-to-end maritime intelligence platform designed to detect, track, classify, and forecast the drift of floating marine plastic debris, container cargo losses, and industrial nurdle spills across the Kerala and Southern Tamil Nadu coastal corridors.

The system fuses multi-spectral optical satellite imagery (Copernicus Sentinel-2), all-weather synthetic aperture radar (Copernicus Sentinel-1 SAR), hyperspectral polymer absorption curves (PRISMA/EnMAP), and Lagrangian hydrodynamic particle drift modeling powered by INCOIS (Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services) ocean current and monsoon wind vectors.

Built specifically to operate on standard consumer hardware, the processing pipeline utilizes windowed raster streaming and Scene Classification Layer (SCL) water-masking to enforce a strict memory ceiling under 1.5 GB RAM. The platform translates complex geospatial rasters into an interactive, real-time command dashboard designed for environmental authorities, port operators, and coastal disaster management agencies.
